title: Nagata passes down along a separable extension of discrete valuation rings
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes an extension A in B of discrete valuation rings and asserts that if B is Nagata and the extension L/K of fraction fields is separable, then A is Nagata (source lines 35666-35671). The proof first recalls the criterion that a discrete valuation ring is Nagata exactly when it is N-2, so it suffices to show that for a finite purely inseparable extension K_1/K the integral closure A_1 of A in K_1 is finite over A (proof lines 35674-35677). The substantive step is the field-theoretic observation: since L/K is separable and K_1/K is purely inseparable, the algebra L tensor_K K_1 is a field, by the reducedness and radicial-integrality lemmas (proof lines 35678-35681). Letting B_1 be the integral closure of B in that field, Nagata-ness of B makes B_1 finite over B; since B tensor_A A_1 is contained in B_1 and B is Noetherian, that subring is finite over B (proof lines 35682-35685). The final step is descent: because A -> B is faithfully flat, finiteness of B tensor_A A_1 over B implies finiteness of A_1 over A, by the descent lemma for properties of modules (proof lines 35685-35687). The non-routine content is the field-theoretic identification of the base change as a field, which is what allows Nagata-ness of B to be tested there, together with the faithful flat descent at the end.
